answer.rationale: Primary contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew and the line has no buffer at 94% volume, so delivery risk dominates. Renewing the incumbent integration (c1) avoids migration risk; renegotiating at this renewal (c4) plus a possible multi-year volume structure (c6) is the only path that can cut TCO without adding a second onboarding or a vendor cutover. Switch/second-source/defer are rejected: 14 days and zero buffer make a primary move or a gap after expiry an outage risk, and c5’s month-to-month deferral was for a non-critical service. Unverified whether benchmarking can approach the 18% mandate; that remains uncertain pending the c4 source and the incumbent’s counter.
